entries.name: AG2 (AutoGen)
entries.use_for: Build conversational multi-agent systems where agents talk to each other and use tools.
entries.why: Community continuation of the original AutoGen; established multi-agent conversation patterns.
entries.summary: Python agent framework (continuation of AutoGen) whose v1 is a protocol-driven package imported as ag2: agents that call tools, human-in-the-loop pauses, and multi-agent orchestration over a Network with typed channels. The classic autogen API now lives in ag2-classic.
entries.best_for: Multi-agent systems in Python where agents converse and use tools, or migrating AutoGen-style projects.
entries.not_for: v1 no longer ships the autogen import or ConversableAgent/GroupChat; those are in ag2-classic. Python only.

entries.name: Agent Development Kit (ADK)
entries.use_for: Build, evaluate and deploy code-first agents and multi-agent systems.
entries.why: Google's official agent toolkit; built-in eval, dev UI and deployment to Vertex/Cloud Run, model-agnostic.
entries.summary: Code-first Python framework for building, evaluating and deploying agents. Offers a graph-based workflow runtime (routing, fan-out, loops, retry), a Task API for delegation, multi-agent hierarchies, tools including OpenAPI and MCP, and deployment tooling. Optimized for Gemini but model-agnostic.
entries.best_for: Python agents and multi-agent systems with built-in eval, dev UI and Google Cloud deployment.
entries.not_for: Tightest integration is with Google/Gemini and Vertex; heavier than minimal agent libraries. Python (other languages have separate repos).

entries.name: Agent Reach
entries.use_for: Give a coding agent read and search access to the web, YouTube, Twitter/X, Reddit, GitHub, RSS and Chinese platforms.
entries.why: Very widely adopted; free backends with automatic fallbacks and a doctor command.
entries.summary: One CLI that gives any command-line agent (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw) internet access: read web pages, YouTube subtitles and search, RSS, GitHub, Twitter/X, Reddit, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu and more. Each platform has a preferred and a fallback backend, and `agent-reach doctor` shows what works.
entries.best_for: Letting an agent read and search social platforms and the web for free, for research or monitoring.
entries.not_for: Users who need English-first docs (the README is mainly Chinese), or platforms that require logins you do not want to hand over (Reddit and full Twitter search need cookies).

entries.name: Agent S
entries.use_for: Build computer-use agents that operate desktop GUIs like a human
entries.why: Open computer-use agent framework with state-of-the-art OSWorld results; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Open-source computer-use agent framework that sees the screen and operates a real GUI with mouse and keyboard on macOS, Windows and Linux, with OpenAI, Anthropic and open-weight models. Agent S3 reports 72.60% on OSWorld.
entries.best_for: Research and prototypes of agents that automate arbitrary desktop and web apps without per-app APIs.
entries.not_for: Research framework: GUI automation is slow, costly and fragile versus API integration. A hosted product (Sai) is promoted for production use.

entries.name: AgentScope
entries.use_for: Build transparent, observable multi-agent applications with MCP and tool support.
entries.why: Actively developed (33k stars) multi-agent framework from Alibaba with strong visibility into agent runs.
entries.summary: Agent framework from Alibaba that leans on model reasoning and tool use rather than rigid prompts. Provides agents, MCP and tool support, TeamPipeline leader/member delegation, model routing, SOPs and an agent service with realtime voice (experimental).
entries.best_for: Observable multi-agent apps in Python with MCP, team delegation and a deployable service layer.
entries.not_for: Several features are marked experimental. Python only; ecosystem is smaller than LangChain.

entries.name: Agno
entries.use_for: Build multi-agent systems with memory, knowledge and tools, plus a runtime to serve them.
entries.why: Fast-growing Python agent framework (~43k stars) with teams, memory, RAG and a production runtime.
entries.summary: Framework and runtime for agent platforms: build agents with the SDK, serve them via AgentOS (50+ API endpoints, SSE/websockets, sessions, memory, knowledge, traces in your database) and manage via a UI. Includes 100+ toolkits, RBAC, approvals and scheduling.
entries.best_for: Taking Python agents to production as a self-hosted service with storage, auth and chat interfaces.
entries.not_for: More platform than library; heavier than a simple agent loop. Python and container-based deployment assumed.

entries.name: ART
entries.use_for: Train multi-step agents with reinforcement learning (GRPO)
entries.why: Agent Reinforcement Trainer: plugs RL fine-tuning into existing agent code to improve reliability on real tasks.
entries.summary: Reinforcement-learning framework that trains multi-step agents with GRPO. An OpenAI-compatible client plugs into existing Python code while a server handles training, locally or on an ephemeral GPU environment; integrates with W&B, Langfuse and OpenPipe.
entries.best_for: Improving agent reliability on a real task by training an LLM with RL from experience.
entries.not_for: Needs GPU training infrastructure and a reward/eval design; not for prompt-only agent building.

entries.name: CAMEL
entries.use_for: Build role-playing multi-agent systems and agent societies in Python
entries.why: One of the earliest multi-agent frameworks; 238 contributors, toolkits, memory and workforce orchestration, Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Open-source multi-agent framework and research community for role-playing agent societies, with ChatAgent, toolkits, memory, workforce orchestration, synthetic data generation and many cookbooks. Apache-2.0.
entries.best_for: Research and prototyping of role-playing or multi-agent systems and synthetic datasets in Python.
entries.not_for: Research-oriented with a broad surface; heavier than minimal frameworks for a simple single agent.

entries.name: Claude Agent SDK (Python)
entries.use_for: Build agents on the same harness that powers Claude Code, with tools, MCP and hooks.
entries.why: Official Anthropic SDK (~8k stars) exposing Claude Code's agent loop, file and shell tools and MCP support.
entries.summary: Python SDK exposing the Claude Code agent harness: query() streams messages, ClaudeSDKClient supports conversations, with built-in tools, custom tools, MCP and hook callbacks (for example blocking a Bash command).
entries.best_for: Building Python agents on Claude Code's loop with file, shell and MCP tools.
entries.not_for: Claude-only and relies on the Claude Code runtime; not provider-agnostic.

entries.name: CrewAI
entries.use_for: Orchestrate teams of role-based agents that collaborate on tasks.
entries.why: Popular multi-agent framework (60k stars) with a simple crew/task model, independent of LangChain.
entries.summary: Python multi-agent framework with role-based Crews of agents and event-driven Flows, built independently of LangChain with a lightweight core. A separate paid enterprise platform adds tracing and a control plane.
entries.best_for: Role-based agent teams collaborating on tasks with a simple crew/task model.
entries.not_for: Observability, control plane and support are in the paid CrewAI AMP product. Python only.

entries.name: DSPy
entries.use_for: Program LLM pipelines and agents declaratively and optimise their prompts automatically.
entries.why: Stanford's framework (~39k stars) that replaces hand-written prompts with optimisable modules.
entries.summary: Framework for programming rather than prompting LMs: write compositional Python modules and use optimizers to tune prompts and weights for classifiers, RAG pipelines or agent loops.
entries.best_for: Systematic quality improvement of LLM pipelines with metrics and optimization instead of hand-tuned prompts.
entries.not_for: Requires eval data/metrics and a different mental model; unnecessary for simple one-off calls. Python only.

entries.name: LangChain
entries.use_for: Build LLM apps and agents with a huge library of model, tool and retriever integrations.
entries.why: The most widely adopted LLM framework (148k stars, 3.7k contributors); largest integration ecosystem.
entries.summary: Python framework for LLM apps and agents with standard interfaces and a large integration library for models, embeddings, vector stores, retrievers and tools. Higher-level Deep Agents and low-level LangGraph build on it.
entries.best_for: Rapid LLM app development needing many provider and vector store integrations.
entries.not_for: Large abstraction surface and frequent API change; simple apps may prefer provider SDKs. LangSmith tracing is a separate hosted product.

entries.name: LangChain.js
entries.use_for: Build LLM apps and agents in TypeScript with LangChain's integrations.
entries.why: JS/TS port of LangChain (~3M weekly npm downloads) with hundreds of model, tool and vector store integrations.
entries.summary: TypeScript/JavaScript version of LangChain with a standard interface for agents, models, embeddings and vector stores and many integrations. Deep Agents and LangGraph.js are companion packages.
entries.best_for: JS/TS LLM apps and agents needing broad integrations.
entries.not_for: Abstraction-heavy; for lighter needs consider the Vercel AI SDK or provider SDKs. Integrations are separate packages.

entries.name: LangChain4j
entries.use_for: Build LLM apps, tools and agents on the JVM with a unified provider API
entries.why: The de facto Java LLM/agent library: 500+ contributors, 20+ model providers, RAG, tools and Spring/Quarkus integrations.
entries.summary: Java library for LLM apps on the JVM with unified APIs over 20+ LLM providers and 30+ embedding stores, plus prompt templating, chat memory, function calling, agents and RAG. Examples for plain Java, Quarkus and Spring Boot.
entries.best_for: Java and JVM teams adding LLM, RAG or agent features.
entries.not_for: JVM only. For Python/JS use other libraries; some features track LangChain concepts rather than Spring AI conventions.

entries.name: LangGraph
entries.use_for: Build stateful, long-running agents as graphs with persistence, human-in-the-loop and streaming.
entries.why: Low-level, controllable orchestration with durable state; the production agent runtime of the LangChain ecosystem.
entries.summary: Low-level orchestration framework for stateful, long-running agents modeled as graphs, with durable execution, human-in-the-loop state inspection, short and long-term memory, streaming and deployment infrastructure.
entries.best_for: Controllable production agent workflows that need persistence, resumption and human oversight.
entries.not_for: Low-level: you design the graph yourself. Debugging UI is LangSmith, a separate product; for quick agents consider higher-level packages.

entries.name: Letta
entries.use_for: Run stateful agents with long-term memory that persist across sessions.
entries.why: Formerly MemGPT (~25k stars); agents with self-editing memory, served via an API server.
entries.summary: Stateful agents with self-editing long-term memory (formerly MemGPT). Current source lives in letta-code, offering a terminal UI, App Server, desktop and web apps, channels and an Agent SDK; the old V1 API server is archived.
entries.best_for: Persistent agents with memory across sessions via CLI, server or SDK.
entries.not_for: This repo is mostly a pointer; the retired V1 server is on an archive branch. Cloud features are hosted.

entries.name: LiveKit Agents
entries.use_for: Build realtime voice/video AI agents on WebRTC
entries.why: Production voice-agent framework from LiveKit with turn detection, telephony and many provider plugins; 540+ contributors.
entries.summary: Framework for realtime voice and video AI agents on WebRTC. Mix STT, LLM, TTS and realtime APIs; includes job dispatch, telephony, semantic turn detection, MCP support and a test framework.
entries.best_for: Production voice agents including phone calls, with low-latency streaming.
entries.not_for: Built around LiveKit (WebRTC server and clients). Python (JS in AgentsJS); heavier than a text-only agent setup.

entries.name: Mastra
entries.use_for: Build AI agents, workflows and RAG in TypeScript with memory, evals and tracing.
entries.why: Leading TypeScript agent framework (29k stars, ~700 contributors); integrates with the Vercel AI SDK.
entries.summary: TypeScript framework for AI apps and agents: model routing across 40+ providers, agents, graph-based workflows (.then/.branch/.parallel), human-in-the-loop suspend/resume, memory/context management, RAG, evals and tracing. Integrates with React, Next.js and Node.
entries.best_for: TypeScript teams building agents and workflows with memory, evals and observability.
entries.not_for: TypeScript only; a full framework, heavier than the plain AI SDK for simple chat features.

entries.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
entries.use_for: Build and orchestrate agents and multi-agent workflows in Python or .NET.
entries.why: Microsoft successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen; first-class .NET and Python support.
entries.summary: Open multi-language framework for production agents and multi-agent workflows in .NET and Python (Go in a separate repo), with middleware, multiple provider support and hosting patterns. Successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen.
entries.best_for: Teams on .NET or Python needing production agents with Microsoft/Azure ecosystem support.
entries.not_for: Go SDK lives elsewhere. Strongest in Microsoft/Azure ecosystems; heavier than minimal SDKs.

entries.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
entries.use_for: Build multi-agent workflows with handoffs, guardrails and tracing in a lightweight SDK.
entries.why: Official OpenAI agents SDK; minimal primitives, provider-agnostic, 30k stars and 400+ contributors.
entries.summary: Lightweight SDK for multi-agent workflows with agents, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tools (functions, MCP, hosted), human in the loop, tracing, realtime and voice agents. Supports Responses and Chat Completions APIs and 100+ LLMs.
entries.best_for: Simple multi-agent apps with handoffs, guardrails and tracing, with OpenAI or other providers.
entries.not_for: Best tuned for OpenAI APIs; some features (hosted tools, realtime) are OpenAI-specific. Python only.

entries.name: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS)
entries.use_for: Build multi-agent workflows with handoffs, guardrails and tracing in TypeScript.
entries.why: Official TS version of the OpenAI Agents SDK (~2.2M weekly npm downloads); also supports voice agents.
entries.summary: TypeScript version of the OpenAI Agents SDK: agents, sandbox agents, realtime/voice agents, handoffs, tools, guardrails, human in the loop, sessions and tracing; provider-agnostic.
entries.best_for: TypeScript or Node multi-agent workflows with guardrails and tracing, including voice.
entries.not_for: Some capabilities are OpenAI-specific. Smaller ecosystem than LangChain.js.

entries.name: Pipecat
entries.use_for: Build realtime voice and multimodal conversational agents
entries.why: Daily-maintained pipeline framework with 360+ contributors and plug-in STT/LLM/TTS and transport services.
entries.summary: Python framework for realtime voice and multimodal agents using composable pipelines of STT, LLM, TTS and transports. Supports multi-agent handoffs and a CLI quickstart.
entries.best_for: Voice assistants, support bots and multimodal conversational apps with pluggable AI services.
entries.not_for: Python only and focused on realtime audio/video; not for text-only agents.

entries.name: PocketFlow
entries.use_for: Tiny 100-line graph framework for agents, workflows and RAG
entries.why: Deliberately minimal, zero-dependency LLM framework that is easy to read and fork; popular base for agent-coded projects.
entries.summary: Minimalist 100-line LLM framework with zero dependencies, expressing agents, workflows and RAG as graphs. Ports exist in TypeScript, Java, C++, Go, Rust and PHP; designed for agentic coding.
entries.best_for: Small, readable foundations you can copy or fork, with no vendor wrappers.
entries.not_for: Deliberately has no built-in integrations (LLM, vector DB, tools); you write them. Not for batteries-included needs.

entries.name: Pydantic AI
entries.use_for: Build type-safe Python agents with validated structured outputs and tool calls.
entries.why: From the Pydantic team; model-agnostic, strongly typed, with dependency injection and evals built in.
entries.summary: Typed Python agent framework from the Pydantic team: model-agnostic agent loop with structured outputs, tools, dependency injection, voice, embeddings and image generation. Companion packages cover evals, graphs and a harness for memory and guardrails.
entries.best_for: Python agents needing validated structured outputs and strong typing.
entries.not_for: Python only; Logfire and Gateway are separate commercial products. Heavier than the Instructor library for pure extraction.

entries.name: Semantic Kernel
entries.use_for: Add AI agents and plugins to .NET, Python or Java apps.
entries.why: Microsoft's model-agnostic SDK (~29k stars), strongest choice for .NET agent and plugin orchestration.
entries.summary: Model-agnostic SDK for agents, plugins and multi-agent orchestration in .NET, Python and Java. Now succeeded by Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0, with a migration guide.
entries.best_for: Maintaining existing Semantic Kernel apps, especially in .NET.
entries.not_for: Microsoft directs new work to Agent Framework; start there for new projects.

entries.name: smolagents
entries.use_for: Build lightweight agents that write and run Python code as their actions.
entries.why: Hugging Face's minimal agent library (~30k stars); code-first agents, any model, sandboxed execution.
entries.summary: Minimal agent library (~1,000 lines of core logic) where CodeAgent writes actions as Python code, with sandboxed execution via Blaxel, E2B, Modal or Docker. Model-, modality- and tool-agnostic with Hub sharing and MCP tools.
entries.best_for: Lightweight code-writing agents with any model and sandboxed execution.
entries.not_for: Code-as-action requires sandboxing for safety; smaller ecosystem than LangChain. Python only.

entries.name: Spring AI Alibaba
entries.use_for: Build graph-based multi-agent workflows in Spring Boot apps
entries.why: Alibaba's agentic framework on top of Spring AI, with graph orchestration and multi-agent patterns for Java teams.
entries.summary: Java framework on Spring AI for agentic, workflow and multi-agent apps: Sequential, Parallel, Routing and Loop agents, graph workflows, context engineering policies, A2A with Nacos, voice agent and MCP support.
entries.best_for: Spring Boot teams building agents and graph workflows, especially in the Alibaba cloud ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Java and Spring only; tied to Spring AI conventions and Alibaba/Nacos integrations.

entries.name: Strands Agents SDK
entries.use_for: Build production agents with a model-driven loop, tools and MCP support.
entries.why: Open-source agent SDK from AWS (Apache-2.0, 300+ contributors); minimal code, any model provider.
entries.summary: Open-source SDK from AWS for building agents in Python and TypeScript with a model-driven loop, tools, structured output, MCP, multi-agent patterns, memory, guardrails, tracing and evals. Runs in your process with no hosted control plane.
entries.best_for: Production agents with minimal code across model providers, including AWS Bedrock.
entries.not_for: You assemble hosting yourself; AWS-leaning examples. Python and TypeScript only.

entries.name: VoltAgent
entries.use_for: Build TypeScript agents with tools, memory, sub-agents and a built-in observability console.
entries.why: Open-source TS agent framework with integrated tracing/debugging console; MIT licensed.
entries.summary: TypeScript agent framework with core runtime, tools, memory, RAG, guardrails, MCP, voice, workflows and supervisor/sub-agent teams, plus the VoltOps console for observability and evals (cloud or self-hosted).
entries.best_for: TypeScript agent apps wanting built-in tracing and a console.
entries.not_for: Some operations features are in the VoltOps console, which has cloud and self-hosted tiers. TypeScript only.
